title: 第25章 三堂会审一第26章 三堂会审二
content_zh:
御史台的大堂上气氛肃杀。
秋日的阳光从高高的窗棂间斜射进来，将大堂上众人的影子拉得又长又淡，投在青砖地面上，像一幅幅被水晕开的墨迹。
大堂正中悬着一块匾额，上书“明镜高悬”四个大字，透着森然不容置疑的威压。
主审官的位置上坐着三个人，正中是刑部侍郎刘梦杰，五十余岁，面容清瘦，颧骨高耸，一双眼睛不大，却精光内敛，像两把藏在鞘中的刀，穿着一身黑色官服，腰间系着金鱼带，坐在那里脊背挺得笔直，像一杆标尺。
左手边是大理寺少卿崔澹，四十出头，嘴角挂着一丝若有若无的笑，那笑容看不出温度，像是画上去的。
右手边是御史中丞卢宏正，年纪最长，须发花白，面容严肃，眉头微蹙，像是已经对这世界的肮脏事看透了却又不得不看。
三司会审，这是本朝审理重大案件的最高规格，刑部主律，大理寺主审，御史台主监，三法司同堂问案，彼此制衡，互为监督。
能启动三司会审的案子，要么关乎社稷安危，要么牵动朝堂根基，杜茂源一案，显然两者都占了。
堂下，杜茂源跪在青砖地面上，穿着一身脏污的白色囚衣，头发散乱，手腕和脚踝上的玄铁镣铐已换成更粗壮的铁链，在地面上盘成一团，像一条蜷缩的蛇。他的膝盖在冰冷的地面上跪了许久，已经开始发麻，但他不敢动，肚子里一颗心七上八下。
大堂两侧立着两排持戟的禁军，甲胄鲜明，面容冷峻，目光如鹰隼般盯着堂下跪着的犯人。再往后是刑部、大理寺、御史台的属官们，一个个正襟危坐，手持法纪文书，目光紧盯堂中，不敢有丝毫懈怠。
堂外的甬道上，杜若和杜欣都被拦在二门之外。她们的身份不允许进入庭审现场，重案的审理，连旁听都需要三品以上的官员，她们这种闺阁女子连门槛都摸不着。
“七娘，你说爹会不会被治罪啊？爹会不会有事啊？”杜欣喃喃，就是个没有主意的寻常妇人。与其说她担心杜茂源的生死，是父女情深，但更多是担心自己的前途，担心杜茂源这棵树倒了，她会被夫家扫地出门。罪臣之后会有什么下场，她不敢想……
杜若没有回答她，目光只盯着庭审的方向。
大堂上，惊堂木响了。
“威武——”
堂威声从两侧的皂隶口中喊出，拖着长长的尾音，在空旷的大堂来回撞击，震得窗棂嗡嗡作响。刘梦杰端坐在正中，目光落在跪在堂下的杜茂源身上，缓缓开口：“堂下何人？”
“罪臣杜茂源。”
“所犯何罪？”
杜茂源的身体微微颤了一下，他知道这一问一答是规矩，是流程，是从大州律里一字一句抄下来的程式，但他也知道这规矩底下藏着的东西比规矩本身要复杂得多。一道圣旨上说他是勾结闽地驻军意图谋反，可那甚至不是判决，只是让审讯开始的令牌。最终定什么罪、判什么刑，全看这三司官员怎么审、怎么议、怎么报。
“罪臣……”他的嘴唇哆嗦了一下，“罪臣勾结闽地驻军，意图不轨。”

声音不大，在空旷的大堂里却听得清清楚楚。崔澹的眉头微微动了一下，嘴角那丝若有若无的笑依然挂在脸上，看不出是满意还是不满意。卢宏正面无表情，只是提笔在面前的案卷上写了几个字，笔尖落在纸上，发出细微的沙沙声。
刘梦杰没有追问，而是从案上拿起一卷文书展开念道：“会昌五年，泾原节度使杜茂源私遣船只，载金银若干，赴闽地，以探亲为名行贿赂之实，船行至东海遇匪，财物尽失。”他顿了一下，目光从文书上抬起来，落在杜茂源身上，“此事你认吗？”
“认。”杜茂源道。
“为何贿赂闽地驻军？”
大堂里安静下来，杜茂源跪在那里，后背的囚衣已经被冷汗湿透，贴在脊背上冰凉。他知道这句话是整个审讯的关键，他怎么回答决定了他最终的罪名是结交外臣还是谋反。
“罪臣……”他的喉咙滚动了一下，“罪臣与闽地驻军并无深交，只是……只是想借他们的关系打通海上的商路。泾原府用度拮据，想为府里谋些生息。”
“商路？”崔澹忽然开了口，“杜节使，你一个内陆节度使要海上的商路做什么？你的辖地在泾原，不靠海，不通漕运，商路打通了，货物从哪里上船？又从哪条路运到你的地盘上？”
杜茂源的脸色白了白，崔澹的问题像一把锥子精准地扎进了他话里的漏洞。他不能说那些货是要送到闽地驻军手里，因为那是坐实了贿赂；他也不能说那些货是要自己贩售的，因为一个内陆节度使私下经营海上贸易同样是违制。
“罪臣……”他的声音发颤，“罪臣是想将泾原的特产运往闽地贩卖，再从闽地采购货物回泾原。虽不靠海，但泾原与京城相近，京城里的货物多半是从东南来的……”
卢宏正开口了，声音沉稳，“你从泾原运特产去闽地，路途数千里，车马劳顿，到了闽地还要转船出海，这一来一回，成本几何，利润几何？你一个节度使放着辖地里的正经营生不做，要来操这份商贾的心？”
杜茂源的额头开始冒汗，他没想到这两个人会问得这么细。在他的预想中，三司会审不过是走个过场，李利民已经答应保他，只要他认下勾结闽地驻军的罪名，把郑柱摘出去，审讯很快就会结束。可他忘了，三司会审不是李利民一个人的，刑部、大理寺、御史台各有各的算盘，各有各的立场。
刘梦杰抬了抬手，制止了崔澹和卢宏正的追问。他看着杜茂源，声音不急不慢：“杜茂源，本官再问你一遍——”
杜茂源抬起头，迎上刘梦杰的目光。
“你贿赂闽地驻军，意欲何为？幕后指使是谁？是不是郑柱？”
大堂里的空气像是被人抽走了一层，所有人都屏住了呼吸。杜茂源的嘴唇剧烈地颤抖着，他看着刘梦杰那张清瘦的脸，看着那双精光内敛的眼睛，忽然意识到这场审讯不是走个过场那么简单。李利民答应保他，但李利民不在台上，台上坐着的是三个人，各有各的立场，各有各的算盘，他们不会因为李利民的一句话就轻轻放过他。
“罪臣……”他一字一顿，脑子在急速运转，“罪臣与闽地驻军勾结，是罪臣一人所为，与他人无关。郑柱对此事毫不知情，从未参与。”
这句话说出口的瞬间，杜茂源觉得自己就像是被人从悬崖上推了下去。他不是在回答问题，他是在念一份早已写好的台词，李利民教他念的，李利民用杜家满门的安危逼他念的。
content_en:
The atmosphere in the lobby of Yushitai was solemn.
The autumn sunlight slants in from the tall window lattice, making the shadows of everyone in the lobby long and thin, casting them on the blue brick floor, like ink stains blurred by water.
There is a plaque hanging in the middle of the lobby, with the four characters "Mingjing hangs high" written on it, which conveys a strong and unquestionable pressure.
There were three people sitting in the seat of the presiding judge. In the middle was Liu Mengjie, the Minister of Justice, who was in his fifties. He had a thin face, high cheekbones, and small eyes, but his eyes were small and restrained, like two knives hidden in sheaths. He was wearing a black official uniform with a goldfish belt around his waist. He sat there with his back straight, like a ruler.
On the left is Cui Dan, the young minister of Dali Temple. He is in his early forties, with a faint smile hanging on the corner of his mouth. There is no warmth in the smile, as if it was painted on.
On the right is Lu Hongzheng, the censor, the oldest, with gray beard and hair, a serious face, and a slightly frowned brow, as if he has seen through the dirty things in this world but has to see it.
The joint trial of three divisions is the highest standard for the trial of major cases in this dynasty. The Ministry of Punishment is in charge, the Dali Temple is in charge of the trial, and the Yushitai is in charge. The three divisions of law investigate the case together, checking and balancing each other, and supervising each other.
Cases that can trigger the joint trial of the three departments are either related to the safety of the country or the foundation of the court. The case of Du Maoyuan obviously involves both.
Downstairs, Du Maoyuan was kneeling on the green brick floor, wearing a dirty white prison uniform, with messy hair. The dark iron shackles on his wrists and ankles had been replaced by thicker iron chains, coiled on the ground like a curled snake. His knees were numb after kneeling on the cold ground for a long time, but he did not dare to move, his heart pounding in his stomach.
On both sides of the hall stood two rows of Imperial Guards holding halberds, with bright armor and stern faces, staring at the kneeling prisoners below the hall like hawks. After that, there are the officials from the Ministry of Punishment, Dali Temple, and Yushitai. They are all sitting upright, holding legal documents and staring at the hall, not daring to slack off in the slightest.
On the corridor outside the hall, Du Ruo and Du Xin were both stopped outside the second door. Their status does not allow them to enter the court hearing. The hearing of serious cases requires officials of third grade or above to even observe. Women in the boudoir like them cannot even touch the threshold.
"Qiniang, do you think dad will be punished? Will something happen to dad?" Du Xin murmured, just an ordinary woman with no idea. She was not so much worried about Du Maoyuan's life and death because of the deep love between father and daughter, but she was more worried about her own future. She was worried that if Du Maoyuan's tree fell, she would be kicked out of her husband's family. She didn't dare to think about what would happen to the guilty minister in the future...
Du Ruo did not answer her, and only stared in the direction of the trial.
In the lobby, the gavel sounded.
"Mighty——"
The majestic voice was shouted from the mouths of the slaves on both sides, with a long tail tone, hitting back and forth in the empty lobby, making the window lattice buzz. Liu Mengjie sat in the middle, his eyes fell on Du Maoyuan who was kneeling in the hall, and he slowly said: "Who is there in the hall?"
"The sinner Du Maoyuan."
"What crime was committed?"
Du Maoyuan's body trembled slightly. He knew that this question and answer was a rule, a process, and a program copied word for word from Dazhou Law, but he also knew that the things hidden under this rule were much more complicated than the rule itself. An imperial edict stated that he had colluded with the Fujian garrison to plot rebellion, but that was not even a verdict, just a token to start the interrogation. The final conviction and sentence all depend on how the officials of these three departments review, discuss, and retaliate.
"The guilty minister..." His lips trembled, "The guilty minister colluded with the garrison in Fujian and had evil intentions."
The sound was not loud, but it could be heard clearly in the empty lobby. Cui Dan's brows moved slightly, and the faint smile at the corner of his mouth was still hanging on his face. It was unclear whether he was satisfied or dissatisfied. Lu Hong was expressionless. He just picked up a pen and wrote a few words on the case file in front of him. The tip of the pen fell on the paper and made a slight rustling sound..
Liu Mengjie did not ask further questions, but picked up a volume of documents from the case, unfolded it and read: "In the fifth year of Huichang, Du Maoyuan, the envoy of Jingyuan Jiedu, privately sent a ship to Fujian, carrying some gold and silver, in the name of visiting relatives to pay bribes. The ship was encountered by bandits in the East China Sea, and all his property was lost." He paused, looked up from the document, and fell on Du Maoyuan, "Do you agree with this?"
"Recognize it," Du Maoyuan said.
"Why bribe the troops stationed in Fujian?"
The lobby fell silent, and Du Maoyuan was kneeling there. The prison clothes on his back were soaked with cold sweat, and they were cold against his back. He knew that this sentence was the key to the entire interrogation, and how he answered it would determine whether he would be charged with befriending foreign ministers or treason.
"The guilty minister..." His throat rolled, "The guilty minister has no close relationship with the Fujian garrison, but... he just wants to use their relationship to open up trade routes on the sea. The Jingyuan Mansion is strapped for money and wants to make some money for the mansion."
"Trade routes?" Cui Dan suddenly spoke, "Envoy Dujie, what do you, an inland envoy, want to do with sea trade routes? Your jurisdiction is in Jingyuan, which is not close to the sea and cannot be transported by water. Now that the trade routes are open, where will the goods get on the ship? And which road will they take to transport them to your territory?"
Du Maoyuan's face turned pale, and Cui Dan's question was like an awl accurately digging into the holes in his words. He could not say that the goods were to be delivered to the garrison in Fujian, because that would be a real bribe; nor could he say that the goods were to be sold by himself, because it was also illegal for an inland Jiedushi to conduct private maritime trade.
"The guilty minister..." His voice trembled, "The guilty minister wants to transport Jingyuan's specialties to Fujian for sale, and then purchase the goods from Fujian back to Jingyuan. Although it is not close to the sea, Jingyuan is close to the capital, and most of the goods in the capital come from the southeast..."
Lu Hongzheng spoke in a calm voice, "You transported specialties from Jingyuan to Fujian. The journey was thousands of miles long, and the carriage and horses were tiring. When you got to Fujian, you had to transfer to the sea. How much did it cost and how much profit did you make? You, a military governor, left the business in the area under your jurisdiction to worry about this merchant?"
Du Maoyuan's forehead started to sweat. He didn't expect these two people to ask such detailed questions. In his expectation, the interrogation of the three divisions was just a formality. Li Limin had promised to bail him out. As long as he admitted the crime of colluding with the Fujian garrison and removed Zheng Zhu, the interrogation would be over soon. But he forgot that the joint trial of the three departments was not Li Limin's alone. The Ministry of Punishment, Dali Temple, and Yushitai each had their own calculations and positions.
Liu Mengjie raised his hand to stop Cui Dan and Lu Hongzheng from questioning. He looked at Du Maoyuan and said in an unhurried voice: "Du Maoyuan, I will ask you again -"
Du Maoyuan raised his head and met Liu Mengjie's gaze.
"What do you want to do by bribing the Fujian garrison? Who is behind the scenes? Is it Zheng Zhu?"
The air in the lobby seemed to have been sucked out, and everyone held their breath. Du Maoyuan's lips trembled violently. He looked at Liu Mengjie's thin face and those bright and reserved eyes, and suddenly realized that this interrogation was not just a formality. Li Limin promised to protect him, but Li Limin was not on the stage. There were three people sitting on the stage, each with his own position and his own calculations. They would not let him go lightly just because of Li Limin's words.
"The guilty minister..." He spoke slowly, his mind racing rapidly, "The guilty minister colluded with the garrison in Fujian. It was committed by the guilty minister alone and had nothing to do with anyone else. Zheng Zhu had no knowledge of this matter and had never participated."
The moment these words were spoken, Du Maoyuan felt as if he had been pushed off a cliff. He was not answering questions, he was reading a script that had already been written. Li Limin taught him to read it, and Li Limin forced him to read it because of the danger of the Du family.
